meta.title: Large-mapping half-flow exhausts its processing group
meta.faultOneLine: ASN mapping half-flow payloads 3x normal exhaust heap in processing group opsfin-01-neo-odes-large

diagnosis.incident_summary: ASN integration into S4 has been stalled since about 06:15 UTC: GLBL_SAPS4HANA_SAPS4HANA_ASN_INT exchanges sit INPROGRESS at half-flow 2/4 (82,900 by 08:30) while the opsfin-01-neo-odes-large processing group runs at ~99% heap with OOM restarts; the first symptom was a P4 heap alert at 05:10.

hypotheses.cause: Oversized ASN payloads (following the 04:52 STO batch release) are exhausting heap in the opsfin-01-neo-odes-large processing group, causing GC thrash, OOM restarts and a growing consumer backlog.

supports.why: Average ASN_INT payload starts rising at 05:10 (47 KB vs 40 KB baseline), the same minute the heap rule fires.
Payload reaches 119 KB, about 3x baseline, by 06:30 and then plateaus at 121 KB; heap tracks the same climb.
A 3,850-STO batch was released from S4 at 04:52 with ASN generation requested, ahead of the payload growth.
After the 06:35 OOM restart heap drops to 47%, but it is back at 84% by 06:50 (e-0188) and ~99% by 07:10: regrowth in minutes, driven by workload rather than hours of accumulation.
Lag rises on this one group only, starting 06:00, once heap is above 88% and GC pauses exceed 570 ms.

contradicts.why: Message inflow is lower than the same 5-minute window last Thursday (111 vs 174), so this is not more messages. That is why the evidence points to size, not volume.
The batch release is only correlated in time with the payload growth; nothing in the pack states that this batch produced the oversized messages.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: A per-message size record showing normal payload sizes on this flow during 05:10-06:30 would move weight to the leak hypothesis; a record linking the 04:52 batch to the oversized message would raise confidence to High.

hypotheses.cause: A slow, time-based heap leak in the processing-group runtime, independent of payload size.

supports.why: The first symptom is a heap rule hit on the group's pods at 05:10: a heap climb is real and started before any lag or stalled exchange.
Heap sits at 96-98% with ~880 ms GC pauses on all three pods by 06:30, consistent with either a leak or sustained oversized allocations.

contradicts.why: Heap starts rising only after payload size does, and payload size rises in lockstep (47 to 121 KB); a runtime leak would not track message size.
Heap regrows from 47% to ~99% within about 30 minutes of a restart; a slow leak would take hours to rebuild.
Lag was zero on every group at baseline, with the same code and pod versions, until the 04:52 batch.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: A heap histogram showing long-lived retained objects unrelated to the ASN mapping, or a change record deploying new runtime code to this group, would raise it.

hypotheses.cause: S4 (the target) is slow to accept ASNs, so half-flow 2 backs up and the pods fill with waiting exchanges.

supports.why: Exchanges wait at half-flow 2/4 and none has exited it, which is also what a slow downstream would look like.

contradicts.why: The heap climb starts at 05:10, before any exchange is stuck at 2/4 (first sampled at 06:30, e-0161). A downstream stall would show waiting exchanges first, then memory pressure.
The saturation signature (heap 98%, GC pauses ~880 ms) is on the ESB pods; no timeout or 5xx rule hit against S4 appears in the incident window.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: S4 response-time records showing elevated latency or rejections for ASN creation from 06:00 would raise it.

ruled_out.reason: Lag is 0 on the six other processing groups throughout (e-0118, e-0244); only the group that hosts this half-flow is behind.

ruled_out.candidate: Load or volume surge on the ASN flow
ruled_out.reason: Inflow is below last Thursday's for the same window (e-0245), and the early baseline check (e-0005) shows the same pattern.
Lag was already rising at 06:00 (e-0118), and the six other groups share the registry without any lag. The change (e-0144) is an approved standard change unrelated to this group.

ruled_out.candidate: Standing host alerts: SGLORHIPQETLPC1 swap 90% and FRHIPGQAMFTSI01 CPU 98%
ruled_out.reason: Both are recurring non-production host alerts (e-0007, e-0027) on ETL and QA MFT hosts, present before the incident window and unrelated to the ESB pods.

ruled_out.candidate: Background mapping and SOAP alerts on SAPTR_FOM and SFDC_CX flows
ruled_out.reason: Different projects and different error strings (e-0015, e-0018: a target timeout and a missing 'Plant' field), present at baseline; none touches the ASN flow.

checks.action: Check average ASN message size and heap for the group over the last 3 hours
checks.command: Sonar: filter exchange:"GLBL_SAPS4HANA_SAPS4HANA_ASN_INT" and event.code:IFP_MAP001, chart avg(message.size) per 5 min; overlay heap_pct for hip-esb-odes-large pods
checks.if_result_a: Payload ~3x baseline since ~05:00, tracking heap: supports hypothesis 1
checks.if_result_b: Payload flat near 40 KB while heap climbs: supports the runtime-leak hypothesis 2

checks.action: Describe the consumer group and compare lag across partitions and other groups
checks.if_result_a: All partitions lag evenly with consumers restarting/rebalancing: confirms consumer-side saturation (hypotheses 1 or 2)
checks.if_result_b: Lag concentrated on a few partitions or a leader-election gap: points at brokers, which this data argues against

checks.action: Take a heap class histogram from the pod with the most restarts
checks.command: kubectl exec -n hip-cloud-esb hip-esb-odes-large-21bd1b21b-rkxkb -- jcmd 1 GC.class_histogram | head -30
checks.if_result_a: Dominated by ASN mapping buffers / large byte arrays: supports hypothesis 1
checks.if_result_b: Dominated by long-lived cache or listener objects unrelated to the mapping: supports hypothesis 2

checks.action: Confirm S4 ASN creation latency for the same window
checks.command: S4 monitoring: response time and reject count for the ASN inbound service, 05:30-08:30 UTC
checks.if_result_a: Normal latency, no rejects: rules out hypothesis 3

downstream_degraded: S4 ASN creation for stock transport orders
blast_radius.business_objects_at_risk: ASNs for the 3,850 STOs released at 04:52 and later; 82,900 ASN exchanges INPROGRESS at half-flow 2/4 at 08:30 (hourly report)

recovery.proposal: Move GLBL_SAPS4HANA_SAPS4HANA_ASN_INT_02_ESB to the larger heap-tuned processing group (or raise heap on opsfin-01-neo-odes-large), let lag drain, then repush the stuck ASN exchanges from S4. Do not rely on in-place replay: L1's replay of 5 exchanges left them INPROGRESS at 2/4 (e-0378).
recovery.risk: Repush can create duplicate ASNs in S4 for exchanges that partially completed; pod restarts or a half-flow move drop in-flight work; moving the half-flow needs a deployment during business hours.
recovery.rollback: Revert the half-flow to its previous processing-group assignment (configuration revert), pause the repush and let S4 de-duplicate on ASN number before resuming.

diagnosis.post_incident_note: #01 -Analysis/Root cause: [Hypothesis, pending checks] ASN payload size ~3x baseline from 05:10 after the 04:52 STO batch exhausted heap in opsfin-01-neo-odes-large (heap ~99%, GC pauses >1 s, OOM restarts 06:35 and 06:52); lag on the group's topic reached 82,922 while lag on the six other groups stayed 0; 82,900 ASN exchanges INPROGRESS at half-flow 2/4 at 08:30. #02-Resolution/Flow state: [Proposed, awaiting approval] move the ASN half-flow to the larger processing group, drain lag, repush ASNs from S4. #03-Doc used: NA #04- Related records (PRB, Change, Incident, RITM...): INC10790101 and children INC10790311-313; no related change record found (CHG4400202 reviewed and excluded).

diff.changed_summary: The late Sonar batch records that the 04:52 STO batch arrived as a single ASN message 3.1x the usual size and drove a 1.4 GB mapping allocation, which supplies the mechanism the payload hypothesis lacked; it moves from Moderate to High and the runtime-leak alternative drops further.
what_changed: e-late-0001 links the 04:52 batch (e-0043) directly to the oversized message: 3,850 STOs delivered in one ASN, line-item count 3.1x the 24 h average. The gap named in hypothesis 1's contradicts column is closed.
The 1.4 GB mapping allocation is on the order of the heap the pods run out of, which explains why heap regrows to ~99% within minutes after each restart (e-0175).
Hypothesis 2 loses its remaining support: the heap climb has an identified workload cause, so it is now very unlikely to be an independent leak.

Recovery is unchanged in action but sharper: the fix is capacity for large mappings (larger processing group / heap), and future large STO batches should be split or routed to the large group by design.

diagnosisAfterOverrides.incident_summary: ASN integration into S4 has been stalled since about 06:15 UTC because a single 3,850-STO batch produced an ASN message 3.1x normal size that exhausted heap in the opsfin-01-neo-odes-large processing group (82,900 exchanges INPROGRESS at 2/4 by 08:30); the first symptom was a P4 heap alert at 05:10.

1.what_would_change_this: Only a record showing the large message was not the one being mapped when heap peaked would lower it now.

2.what_would_change_this: Effectively closed by the late batch; would reopen only if a restart with normal-size messages still regrows to ~99% within minutes.
